hypothesis: Replacing (not preceding) the 4x-unrolled byte reject inside the string-skip for(;;) loop of LineIndex.build (src/indexer/lineIndex.ts on 1d2377e, brief L267-274) with an alignment-gated Uint32Array haszero word loop that stops on any word with a 0x22 or 0x5c lane, plus an empty-view guard (wN === 0 -> shared zero-length EMPTY_U32, so no RangeError on short/unaligned unpooled buffers), will raise the sealed speedup from ~1.62 to ~1.83-1.90 (~1.13-1.15x relative), because removing the reject lets the existing 1-byte tail ('sb > 0x5c -> continue') realign i within 3 bytes after every escape or stop byte, so the word loop actually runs on string bodies. Round 4's 360a642 kept the reject after the word loop; the reject advanced a misaligned i by 4, the ((base + i) & 3) === 0 gate never re-fired, and the change scored 1.590. This is the only change: the escaped-carry branch, the byte tail, the WCLS outer skip, the switch, checkpoints, record pushes, the for-await loop and EOF handling stay byte-identical.

steps.change: In `for await (const raw of handle)`, right after the existing lines `const buf: Buffer = typeof raw === 'string' ? Buffer.from(raw) : (raw as Buffer);`, `const n = buf.length;`, `const chunkBase = totalBytes; // 本 chunk 起始的绝对偏移` (brief ~L255) and before `let i = 0;`, add the per-chunk aligned view: `const base = buf.byteOffset;` `const aOff = base + ((4 - (base & 3)) & 3); // first 4-byte boundary >= base` `const wN = base + n > aOff ? (base + n - aOff) >>> 2 : 0; // full words inside [aOff, base+n)` `const u32: Uint32Array = wN > 0 ? new Uint32Array(buf.buffer, aOff, wN) : EMPTY_U32;`. aOff + 4*wN <= base + n <= buffer.byteLength, so the view never reads past the chunk and never throws.

Verification (no source edits besides steps 1-4). (a) `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npx oxlint src scripts build.mjs --deny-warnings`, `npx prettier --check src/indexer/lineIndex.ts` (run `npx prettier --write src/indexer/lineIndex.ts` first if needed), `node --experimental-transform-types --test src/indexer/__tests__/lineIndex.test.ts src/perf/__tests__/bigFilePerf.test.ts`: all clean/passing. (b) Differential check in a temp dir outside the repo: `git show 1d2377e:src/indexer/lineIndex.ts` into tmp/ref/src/indexer/lineIndex.ts with src/constants.ts and src/parser/jsonParser.ts copied beside it, the candidate into tmp/cand with the same layout; a node --experimental-transform-types script compares checkpoints, totalLines, totalBytes, record endLines/endOffsets and endsWithNewline (and the public lookup results) between ref and cand for: the benchmark-style generated fixture plus edge fixtures (pretty multiline records, CRLF, empty/leading-empty lines, unterminated final line, escaped-quote runs, \\\\ pairs, unicode/emoji, raw newlines inside strings, long strings > 64 B, trailing backslash at EOF inside an unterminated string, dangling depth at EOF); splits whole/1/2/3/7/64/1000 bytes; checkpointInterval 1/3/1024; delivered as Buffer arrays, async iterables, and string chunks; Buffers as subarrays at offsets 0/1/2/3 of a larger ArrayBuffer; unpooled tiny buffers (Buffer.alloc lengths 1-11 and 4095-4099, data placed at the end of the ArrayBuffer so n mod 4 = 1/2/3 and aOff can exceed byteLength). Every case must match and nothing may throw. (c) Serialized (never parallel) at least 5 runs of `node scripts/benchmark-index-build.mjs` on an idle machine; report every score and the median; correctness must be 1 on every run. Accept if the median >= 1.8 (expected 1.83-1.90); if the median lands 1.75-1.80, record it as below target rather than tuning further. Delete the temp dir afterwards.

expected_outcome.rationale: Round-5 isolation with byte-identical sealed-benchmark copies, alternating processes: the replace shape (swarR) scored 1.895/1.882/1.865 vs base 1.643/1.643/1.680; the guarded swarRG scored 1.837/1.871 vs base 1.605/1.640 in the same sweep, and rel-vs-base 1.178 in-process (q1 0.960, q3 1.365). The control swarK (same word loop, reject kept) scored 1.607/1.615/1.617 and exec4 (= 360a642) 1.631/1.631/1.610, which pins the round-4 regression on the kept reject (alignment lockout), not on view allocation or arithmetic. About 75% of fixture bytes are string bytes, so testing 4 per load with one combined branch is the lever. swarRG passed all 576 differential cases; the guard fixes the RangeError swarR/swarK hit on unpooled 5-10 and 4097-4099 byte buffers. Risk: only ~2-5% headroom over 1.8 against ±4-8% run noise, so a single low run near 1.78-1.80 is plausible; the median of >=5 serialized runs is the decision value.

sub_score_expectations.cur_median_mb_s: ~1.13-1.15x the 1d2377e median on the same machine
